title: Lynfield patient triage onramp — intake scratch journal
content:
Intake capture (raw) — do not treat as final

Context
- Customer: Lynfield Community Clinic (multi-site primary care + urgent teletriage).
- Goal: Replace voicemail triage + manual intake with assisted first-touch via LLM-powered assistant routing to nurse triage or self-care instructions.
- Constraint: All PHI must remain inside customer VPC; audit logs retained for 7 years; infrequent but legally required subpoena/exports.
- Desired timeline: pilot in Q4 (10 clinics, limited hours), production H1 next year.

Attendees & roles (call):
- Dr. Miriam Castillo — clinical lead, defines acceptable guidance/limitations
- Rajesh Menon — IT lead (Kubernetes infra + VPN/VPC networking)
- Elliot Zhang — privacy officer (retention/KMS concerns)
- Aisha Patel — Redwood CS (owning integration)

High-level requirements (as heard)
1) Private deployment option: must be in-customer VPC with customer-managed KMS/HSM (no plaintext model or traces leaving VPC).
2) Model variants: prefer smaller quantized models for latency; but clinical safety requires higher-quality base model for complex triage cases.
3) Latency SLO: 95th <= 650ms for interactive triage flows (short prompts). Bulk batch tasks (daily summarization) can be async.
4) Audit: token-level tracing + prompt/response storage encrypted at rest; retention configured per-policy and able to export on-demand.
5) Content filtering / guardrails: integrated rule set and prompt templates that prohibit diagnosis-only statements and require escalation triggers.
6) Throughput: target pilot peak 6 concurrent triage sessions per clinic, 10 clinics => ~60 concurrent sessions; average QPS estimate: 15–25 requests/s across cluster.
7) Data connectors: FHIR read-only to pull patient context (meds, allergies) for context-aware responses — must be mediated and not stored in raw prompt logs.
8) Sync with EHR: only metadata and final disposition (triage level) should be written back, not raw assistant text; EHR writes guarded by nurse confirmation.

Initial technical gotchas / red flags
- KMS/HSM: customer requires key wrapping where Redwood's control plane never sees raw KMS keys. Need design for customer KMS integration into Private deployment.
- FHIR tokens: Lynfield uses short-lived FHIR tokens via internal auth proxy. Need an adapter and re-auth flow for Redwood service calls from private runtime.
- Audit log volume: 60 concurrent sessions x full prompts/responses could blow log retention/cost; propose selective persistence (hashed prompt index + redacted transcript + full transcript kept only for critical cases).
- Clinical safety: Dr. Castillo insists on explicit escalation triggers for any uncertain diagnosis; must surface confidence heuristics from model or fallback policy to human triage.
- On-prem GPU constraints: One site (site 7) has no GPU capacity; will need region routing to hosted or dedicated fallback with IP allowlist. Customer legal may balk at any data leaving VPC — need explicit fallback agreement.

Prompt & guidance sketch (capture for later refinement)
- System prompt (high level): "You are a clinical intake assistant for Lynfield Community Clinic. Use only the patient context provided. Do not provide a definitive medical diagnosis. If the patient reports any red-flag symptoms (chest pain, difficulty breathing, severe bleeding, altered consciousness, suspected stroke signs), instruct immediate emergency care and escalate to a human nurse. When uncertain, ask clarifying questions and recommend escalation. Always include follow-up actions and whether the patient should be scheduled for nurse triage."
- Example user brevity: "I have a cough and fever 2 days" => Assistant should ask: onset, high-risk conditions, oxygenation concerns, red-flag screening.

Minimal test prompts to include in pilot perf/safety evals:
- short simple: "Sore throat, mild fever, no other symptoms"
- complex multi-condition: "Diabetic, chest pressure intermittent, dizziness when standing, started today"
- PHI masking check: include explicit MRN-like token to ensure logs redaction pipeline functions.

Operational plan (draft)
- Phase 0 (next 4w): integration design review — network, KMS model, FHIR adapter, log redaction plan.
- Phase 1 (8w): private runtime deploy in staging VPC for 2 clinics. Include tracing, small model quantized path + canary to higher-quality model for complex prompts.
- Phase 2 (pilot, 12w): 10 clinics limited hours, monitor latency/cost/clinical escalations. Run weekly human-in-the-loop QA.
- Rollout criteria: false-negative escalation rate <= 1% (clinical defined), latency SLO met for 95p, audit exports validated.

Cost/size heuristic (rough, ballpark)
- Model options: 7B quantized (low latency), 13B quantized (mid), 70B float/8-bit (high-quality fallback).
- Estimated steady-state infra: pilot -> 4–6 GPU nodes (A100-equivalent) depending on batching and KV cache; dedicated capacity may be requested.

Open questions / actions to answer on follow-up
- Legal: confirm whether any minimal set of de-identified logs can be mirrored to Redwood for debugging under DPA (Elliot to confirm).
- KMS: can Lynfield provide a cloud KMS with key-usage APIs we can call from runtime, or do they require HSM appliances on-prem? (Rajesh to confirm)
next_steps: Share draft prompt templates + initial safety rules with Dr. Castillo by 2025-06-07
Prototype FHIR read-only adapter (auth proxy) — assign to eng-integration (Elliot to triage)
Cost-estimate deck for dedicated vs private fallback — Redwood finops to draft
Confirm legal DPA log constraints and export workflow — follow up with Elliot
